To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the DIA problem can be solved using a spatially varying PSF, photometric scale factor or sky background.
the mixed-resolution delta kernels provide a good solution to the least-squares system and that the spatially varying photometry is important for wide-field imaging.

we present the first DIA framework that allows for a spatially varying PSF, photometric scale factor or differential sky background, we introduce mixed-resolution delta basis kernels, we present several optimizations for constructing the least-squares system, we present the first implementation of DIA with a spatially varying scale factor and we demonstrate the performance of our DIA algorithm on simulated and on real data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an algorithm for DIA with an extended set of parameters that can be tuned by the user.
the development of a DIA framework that can be applied to a wide range of astronomical data and which is sufficiently flexible to be adapted to a wide range data analysis problems.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we believe we have provided a framework which is sufficiently general to address most DIA problems, and that we have also provided some useful tools for implementing the framework.

we have developed a framework for the construction of the DIA least-squares matrix, and have introduced a number of new ideas and optimizations to make DIA software more flexible and more computationally efficient.
we have presented a general framework for DIA which allows the user to choose between a variety of basis functions for the PSF, photometric scale factor, and differential sky background.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the DIA framework presented in our paper is sufficiently general to allow for the implementation of any of the existing DIA algorithms, as well as for the development of new ones.
DIA can be formulated as a least-squares problem in which a number of parameters can be spatially varying and which can be optimized using the mixed-resolution delta kernel basis functions.
DIA is a well-understood and well-developed subject, but it has not yet reached its full potential in terms of the flexibility of its implementation.
